# PADDLE_MEASUREMENTS — Phase 2.1 cell P runtime/cost telemetry

```
STATUS: MEASURED — regenerated entirely by tools.paddle_vast measure's own instruments,
        over the real SSH tunnel to the Vast.ai RTX 5090, at closure-2's tip
DATE: 2026-09-02
FIXTURE: tests/paddle_synthetic.py (build_ledger_page / render_image_pdf) — SYNTHETIC ONLY,
         never a real statement, never Bank Statements/ or tests/corpus_cache/ content
```

**Superseded.** Every number in this file was regenerated by a fresh live run once the Vast.ai
instance became reachable again; the historical numbers this file previously carried (hand-collected
GPU/RSS figures, a mislabelled byte count, and a lifecycle that needed an undocumented manual token
export) are gone from this file. The three defects that produced them were already fixed in code
during the first closure — this run is the fresh live re-proof that was owed, using the corrected
lifecycle exactly as documented, with no manual step.

## MAJOR-4 remote-half proof (session token over the SSH forward)

`start` minted/reused the session token on file, exported it to the remote worker's environment,
and every later command in the documented sequence (`status`'s probe, the live pytest, `measure`)
authenticated against `/health`, `/version` and `/ocr` with **no manual `export
PADDLE_WORKER_TOKEN=...` step**. `status` showed `probe.available: true` / `reason: "ok"`
immediately after `tunnel-up`, and `measure` completed 21 authenticated `/ocr` requests (1 cold +
20 warm, plus the `verify_identity` `/version` call before them) without a single 401.

## Real inference proof (MAJOR-1/D9 boundary)

A dedicated two-run probe (`read_document` called twice on the identical synthetic PDF bytes,
`data_scope="synthetic"`, over the live tunnel) confirmed:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| pages returned | 1 (non-empty) |
| word_count (run 1 / run 2) | 36 / 36 |
| `evidence.runtime` identity fields | equal to the pins above, in both runs |
| `evidence_sha256` (run 1) | `BB28AD14B38ADDFF795038D0C93B824E80A3CFEE42A00F5CD1A1E674AE85605A` |
| `evidence_sha256` (run 2) | `BB28AD14B38ADDFF795038D0C93B824E80A3CFEE42A00F5CD1A1E674AE85605A` |
| stable across the two runs | **yes** |

`tests/test_paddle_live.py -m live`: **1 passed**, `EXIT=0` (asserts non-empty pages, `word_count >
0`, the three identity fields, and a stable `document_sha256` across the two calls it makes; the
evidence_sha256-equality figure above comes from the dedicated probe run alongside it, since the
committed live test does not itself assert sha equality — PaddleOCR is not contractually required
to be bit-identical run to run, only this pipeline's own bookkeeping is, and this run's OCR output
happened to be bit-identical too).

## Fixture

An 8-row synthetic ledger page (`tests.paddle_synthetic.build_ledger_page(n_rows=8)`),
rasterised to an image-only PDF at 300 dpi (the D5-pinned raster dpi) and re-encoded as PNG:
2,550 x 3,300 px.

## Cold vs. warm latency

Measured by `tools.paddle_vast measure` itself, immediately after a fresh `stop` + `start` (the
worker's own `/version` reported `model_loaded: false` at measurement start — a genuine cold load,
not a re-measurement of an already-warm worker):

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| cold end-to-end (local rasterise + transfer + infer + adapt via `client.ocr_page`) | **5,208.3 ms** |
| cold inference only (`timing.inference_ms`, the worker's own model-load + first-forward-pass timer) | **3,844.0 ms** |
| warm median end-to-end, n=20 | **1,872.3 ms** |
| warm p95 end-to-end, n=20 | **2,152.4 ms** |

## Transfer size (per page, this fixture)

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| bytes sent — raw PNG | 253,799 bytes (~248 KiB) |
| bytes sent — actual `/ocr` wire body (base64-inflated, JSON-wrapped; what the request actually costs to send) | 338,489 bytes (~331 KiB) |
| bytes received (JSON response incl. word boxes) | 12,264 bytes (~12 KiB) |

## GPU (produced by `cmd_measure`'s own `_default_gpu_sampler`, polled every 5 requests over SSH)

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| GPU memory used, last sample | 7,692 MiB / 32,607 MiB total |
| GPU memory used, peak across samples | 7,692 MiB |
| GPU utilization, last sample / peak across samples | 0% / 0% (idle between requests — the pipeline serialises inference one request at a time, so a point-in-time sample between requests reads near-zero; it does not capture the burst during the roughly 1.9-5.2 s inference window itself) |
| samples taken | 5 |

## Local peak RSS

`psutil` is not installed in this environment, so `local_peak_rss_mib` reports the honest fallback
string `"not measured (psutil not installed)"` rather than a guess — per design, this instrument
never estimates.

## Runtime / cost

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| `measure`'s own reported wall time (the command's full run: identity check + 1 cold + 20 warm requests) | **59.0 s** |
| worker wall-clock, the measured (second, post-restart) instance — `start` to `stop`, timed around the `measure` invocation | ~123 s (~2.0 minutes) |
| worker wall-clock, the first instance this session (deploy self-check + the live pytest + the evidence-stability probe, stopped before the restart above) | not separately instrumented; the same `check`/`deploy`/`start`-to-`stop` bracket, well under 2 minutes |
| hourly rate | not discoverable from the instance's own manifest and not supplied by Gustavo for this run |
| **cost** | **"rate not measured"** — runtime is reported above; cost is never estimated from an assumed rate |

## What this measures (and does not)

This is the Paddle rung's cost per SYNTHETIC page at 300 dpi on an idle, already-deployed RTX
5090 worker over a warm SSH tunnel. It does not include: model download/first-install time (the
official PP-OCRv5 models were already cached on the host before this measurement — a fresh
instance would pay that cost once), Vast.ai instance provisioning/boot time, or any measurement
against the 13-document legal escalation population (D8: that population is not sent to Vast in
Phase 2.1).

## Commands run (host/port/user/token never shown; the runbook has the full sequence)

```
python -m tools.paddle_vast check
python -m tools.paddle_vast deploy
python -m tools.paddle_vast start
python -m tools.paddle_vast tunnel-up
python -m tools.paddle_vast status
PADDLE_REMOTE_OPT_IN=I_ACCEPT_REMOTE_PAID_PADDLE_OCR python -m pytest tests/test_paddle_live.py -m live -q
PADDLE_REMOTE_OPT_IN=I_ACCEPT_REMOTE_PAID_PADDLE_OCR python <the evidence_sha256 two-run stability probe, ad hoc, not committed>
python -m tools.paddle_vast stop && python -m tools.paddle_vast start   # fresh restart for a genuine cold measurement
PADDLE_REMOTE_OPT_IN=I_ACCEPT_REMOTE_PAID_PADDLE_OCR python -m tools.paddle_vast measure --n-rows 8 --warm-requests 20
python -m tools.paddle_vast stop
python -m tools.paddle_vast tunnel-down
```

Every one of the above (except the ad hoc probe, described in prose here since it is not part of
the committed test/tool surface) ran with `PADDLE_REMOTE_OPT_IN` set ONLY in that command's own
environment — never exported for the shell session. `PADDLE_REMOTE_CUSTOMER_DATA_OPT_IN` was never
set. The final `status` after `stop`/`tunnel-down` confirmed `probe.available: false` (worker
process gone) and `tunnel_running: false` — nothing from this run was left running, locally or
remotely.

Fail-closed probe on the same machine (synthetic bytes): `data_scope="customer"` without
`PADDLE_REMOTE_CUSTOMER_DATA_OPT_IN` → `PaddleRefused: remote_customer_data_refused` before any
connection; `data_scope="synthetic"` with the tunnel down → `PaddleTransportError:
paddle_worker_unreachable`. Worker stopped and tunnel torn down afterwards (`tunnel_running: false`).
